    colstat [-d DELIM] [-c COLS] [--max-size N] [--version] [FILE]

Reads a delimited text file from `FILE`, or from standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`,
and prints summary statistics for its columns.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-d DELIM` | Field delimiter: one character, or the word `tab`. Without `-d`: `,`. |
| `-c COLS` | Comma-separated column names, in the order to report them. A name may repeat. Without `-c`: every column in header order. |
| `--max-size N` | Refuse inputs larger than `N` bytes. `N` is a decimal number with an optional suffix: `k` or `K` (1024), `m` or `M` (1024 * 1024), `g` or `G` (1024 * 1024 * 1024). |
| `--version` | Print `colstat VERSION` and exit 0. |

Options may appear in any order. An unknown option, a missing option value, a delimiter longer than
one character, or an invalid size is a usage error.

## Input

- Records end at `\n` or `\r\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
- The first record is the header and names the columns. Column names are compared exactly
  (case and blanks count). When a name occurs twice in the header, the first occurrence is used.
- A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""`
  stands for one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks inside it are part of the field. Any text
  after the closing quote, up to the next delimiter, is appended to the field.
- A record with fewer fields than the header has empty values in the missing columns; extra
  fields are ignored.
- A value is numeric when, after removing spaces and tabs at both ends, it is an optional sign,
  digits with an optional decimal point (at least one digit before or after the point), and an
  optional exponent (`e` or `E`, optional sign, digits). Anything else (empty values, `NA`,
  `inf`, hexadecimal, decimal commas) is not counted.

## Output

One line per selected column, in the selected order:

    NAME: count=N min=... max=... mean=... median=... p90=... stdev=...

- `count` is the number of numeric values. When it is 0 the line ends after `count=0`.
- `mean` is the sum of the values in input order divided by the count.
- `median` is the middle value of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle values.
- `p90` is the nearest-rank 90th percentile: the value at rank `ceil(0.9 * count)` in ascending order.
- `stdev` is the sample standard deviation (divisor `count - 1`), summed in input order; 0 when the
  count is below 2.
- Numbers are printed like C `printf("%.*g")` with `QS_STATS_PRECISION` significant digits
  (defined in `include/qs/stats.h`).

## Exit status

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success. |
| 2 | Usage error, an empty input (no header), or a name in `-c` that is not a column. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 3 | The input is larger than `--max-size`. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 4 | The input cannot be read. |

Error messages go to standard error.
# qcalc

Evaluates arithmetic expressions.

- With `-e EXPR`, evaluates `EXPR` and prints one line.
- Otherwise reads `FILE` (or standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`) and evaluates each line.

- `--version` prints `qcalc VERSION`; `--ops` prints the operation table the program was built with,

The project now builds and meets `docs/BUILDING.md`. I checked this on clean trees at `-j8`, and `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

**What I ran**
- Each target (`all`, `build/lib/libqs.a`, `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc`, `check`, `install`) built from a clean tree at `-j8`, three times each, with no failures.
- `make check` passed: 22 unit tests and 34 golden cases. It also passed under `make DEBUG=1 check`.
- A second `make` with nothing changed ran no compile, archive or link step.
- Changing `VERSION`, a header, or `src/ops.def` rebuilt the dependent objects and the programs.
- `make install` with `PREFIX='/opt/my&pre|fix'` and a `DESTDIR` installed exactly the files and modes the contract lists, and `qs.pc` recorded that prefix. A program built against the installed header and `libqs.a` with `-lm` built and ran.

**Makefile fixes**
- The programs didn't depend on `libqs.a`, and the link line put libraries before the objects. I fixed both.
- `version.h` was never generated. It is now built from `VERSION` with `build-aux/mkversion.sh`.
- There was no header dependency tracking, so I added it. Generated headers are produced before any compile.
- `DEBUG=1` was never recognised, because the makefile tested for `yes`. A stamp file now rebuilds everything when the flags or `CC` change. It also covers a switch from release to debug on an existing `build/`.
- `check` ignored unit-test failures and lost the golden suite's exit status through `tee`. It now runs both suites and fails if either fails.
- `install` didn't install `qcalc.1`, and `qs.pc` was built at make time with whatever `PREFIX` was set then. It is now written during `install` with the given `PREFIX`.
- `all` also built `qs.pc`, which isn't part of the contract, so I removed that.
- I deleted the stale hand-written `include/qs/ops.h`. It disagreed with `ops.def`: wrong `neg` precedence, `pow` left-associative, and no `hypot` or `clamp`.

**Code fixes (all warnings fixed in the code, with no pragmas or `-Wno-` flags)**
- Fixed unused parameters and variables, sign-compare, `%d` used with `size_t`, a missing `<stdlib.h>`, an assignment used as a condition, an unhandled `TOK_END` case, and switch fallthrough.
- Prefix `-` now takes as its operand only the operators that bind strictly tighter than `neg`, as `docs/qcalc.md` says. This gives the same results for the current `ops.def`.
- `--max-size` could overflow silently, for example `16777216g` wrapped to 0. A size too large for `size_t` now saturates, since no input can exceed it. I read the docs as meaning that rather than a usage error, but they don't say.

With no `-c`, `colstat` reports every header column by position. For a duplicated header name, the later column gets its own statistics rather than the first occurrence's. `docs/colstat.md` is ambiguous here and no golden case covers it, so I left that behaviour alone.

I left `build/` removed (`make clean`).
